findings.text: follow-on: the reset call's new path_prefixes argument is not pinned by any test — test_code_cli_forwards_path_prefixes invokes the CLI with --scan-only, which returns before the reset_to branch — so a later edit that drops path_prefixes=list(path_prefixes) or None from this call would shrink the code reset back to facility-wide with a green suite; extending that test to invoke --reset-to with a --path-prefix would close it.

follow-on: test_reset_is_root_scoped_when_root_given and test_reset_matches_root_and_descendants both assert only that paths.py forwards the root list and that render_path_prefix_clause contains the STARTS WITH text for the parameter, so they no longer pin end-to-end that the rendered scope reaches the reset's own WHERE clause for the paths command; the reset-side rendering is pinned in test_reset.py, so the coverage is not lost, only split.

justifications.durability: the prefix behaviour is pinned by unit tests that run in the default suite — test_reset.py::test_reset_path_prefixes_scopes_the_query asserts the rendered clause and the carried parameter, test_reset_without_prefixes_stays_facility_wide asserts no clause and no parameter, test_code_discovered_reset_includes_skipped asserts skipped is a source status, and the three test_paths_pipeline.py tests pin that paths.py passes its --root list through; the gap is that code.py's own reset call (code.py:200) is not exercised — the only code CLI test (test_code_pipeline.py:1537) runs --scan-only and never reaches the reset branch — so dropping path_prefixes from that call would pass the suite.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the gate at the reviewed head — UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex/.venv PYTHONPATH=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/imas-codex-c994bf55fb01/jt60sa-20261005/prefix-scoped-reset uv run --no-sync pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/discovery prints 1157 passed, EXIT=0 (reviewer-gate.log), and reset.__file__ resolves to the reviewed tree; the negative control is real and I reproduced it independently — with `if path_prefixes:` forced False in a scratch copy the query loses `n.path STARTS WITH prefix` and test_reset_path_prefixes_scopes_the_query fails (reviewer-negctl.log), the head arm passing all 22 test_reset.py tests (gate-reset-only.log, EXIT=0). The deduction is that the run's own base arm for the added-failure derivation is not a clean base: gate-head.log's header names 1c81b71ab but the tree it ran carried the node's uncommitted half-change, which is why it lists 3 failures in test_paths_pipeline.py that the head arm does not.
justifications.fit: the new argument is named path_prefixes after the plan's own word, the mechanism is described in the docstring rather than explained by a ticket, the fragment element ids (prefix-scoped-reset-record, prefix-scoped-reset-landing) both open with the node id, and no plan label, version or author attribution appears in any changed symbol, filename or comment.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every element of §14's code-reset node is implemented at 09c995bdc: reset_to_status(reset.py:59) gains path_prefixes and renders render_path_prefix_clause("n","path_prefixes") at reset.py:98, the paths.py inline block is replaced by path_prefixes=root_filter (paths.py:248), code.py passes path_prefixes=list(path_prefixes) or None (code.py:200), CODE_RESET_SPECS["discovered"].source_statuses gains skipped (reset.py:367), signals keeps extra_filter (signals.py:227), and no discover run or remote host was contacted.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses the single renderer render_path_prefix_clause instead of re-spelling the predicate, and in fact removes the last inline spelling of it in paths.py; signals.py's genuinely different scanner predicate is deliberately left on extra_filter, so no second mechanism was forced onto the shared one.
